title: PROP-130 canary is firing 3 consecutive days (ISS-2984). Investigate the RECURRENCE PATTERN — is this a schedule-spacing issue we can fix by spreading poller/workspace-sync/decider further apart in time? Operator's explicit hypothesis: 'we might just need to space out the schedule a bit more'.

context.why_now: Decider's 2026-07-15T02:07Z run flagged PROP-130 status.json two-writer race canary firing on 3 CONSECUTIVE days (ISS-2984). Each firing is followed by poller's self-heal on next daily cycle — the instrumentation-only close of DIRECTIVE-20260711-001 / ISS-2962 is doing what it was designed to do. But 3-consecutive-days is a signal worth investigating: (a) the race may be triggered by a reliable-clockwork condition we didn't understand at ISS-2962 close time, (b) if that condition is timing-adjacent (agents running too close together), simple schedule spacing may eliminate the class without structural surgery.
context.operator_hypothesis: 'We might just need to space out the schedule a bit more.' — Steve, 2026-07-15 morning check-in. Motivation: the race is documented as poller-writes-git-only vs workspace-sync-whole-file-copies-FUSE-view. If those two writers are scheduled close enough together in wall-clock time, FUSE has a stale poller-side view when workspace-sync fires; if they're spaced further apart, FUSE has time to re-sync via dome-mirror's git→FUSE pass before workspace-sync's next FUSE→git pass. Testable + cheap to try if the schedule diagnosis holds.

the_3_recurrences_data.3rd_day_new_incident: Per decider's ISS-2984 title ('status.json field regression on commit 25a4825'), a NEW chimera occurred at 25a4825. Confirm the commit's timestamp + author + which fields regressed vs advanced.

questions_to_answer: Q1 — For each of the 3 chimera-firing incidents (27bf1e4b on 07-12, 25a4825 on 07-15, plus any other in the 30-commit window), identify: commit timestamp (down to the second), commit author agent, which fields advanced, which fields regressed, and what the wall-clock gap was between the last poller push and this culprit push.

Q2 — Is there a deterministic timing pattern? E.g., 'every time workspace-sync's UTC 04:00 slot runs less than N minutes after poller's UTC 00:xx slot commits AND decider's UTC 02:00 slot has written to status.json in between, the race triggers.' Look for a rule.

Q3 — Operator's spacing hypothesis test: if we moved workspace-sync's UTC 04:00 slot to UTC 06:00 (or later), would the race window close? Model this against the 3 observed incidents — would each have been eliminated by the delay?
Q4 — Alternative: is the race triggered by something OTHER than pure agent timing? (e.g., a specific state transition on status.json fields that only certain sequences of writes produce)
part_A_recurrence_forensics.investigation_scope: Read commit history for the 30-commit window that PROP-130 canary looks at. Cross-reference agent scheduled-task cron entries against actual commit timestamps. Do NOT change any schedules in this directive — investigate and recommend.

options_to_consider.label: Space out the schedule (per operator hypothesis)
options_to_consider.shape: If Part A shows the race triggers only when agents run within a certain window of each other, propose specific cron changes to widen the gaps. Update-scheduled-task API calls documented in the PROP.

options_to_consider.label: Accept the 3-per-30-days steady state as pipeline noise
options_to_consider.shape: If Part A shows the race triggers randomly / not tied to schedule, and poller self-heal is bounded (~24h max), just document the steady-state cost + tune the canary's noise threshold if appropriate.
options_to_consider.cost: Zero to trivial (maybe a canary-cadence change).

options_to_consider.label: Add a workspace-sync-side pre-check: skip status.json overwrite if git-side is fresher than FUSE
options_to_consider.shape: Modify workspace-sync's smart_copy for status.json only: read git-side, read FUSE-side, if git's mtime > FUSE's mtime OR git's status.json fields are strictly newer than FUSE's, skip the overwrite. Prevents the chimera even if timing hits the race window.
options_to_consider.cost: Moderate. Workspace-sync hot-path change — needs PROP-051 disaster-class review.

part_B_recommendation.operator_preference: OPT-1 (schedule spacing) is the LOW-COMPLEXITY option operator explicitly hypothesized. If Part A supports it, ship OPT-1 (or propose it as PROP with cron updates). OPT-2 (accept) is legitimate close if the race is not schedule-attributable. OPT-3 (workspace-sync change) is a fallback only if neither of the first two work.

part_C_ship_or_follow_up.if_OPT_1_supported: Ship a PROP with concrete cron updates + call the scheduled_tasks update_scheduled_task tool from operator's approval. Tinker MAY author the PROP + provide the operator with the exact update-task calls to make.
part_C_ship_or_follow_up.if_OPT_2_supported: Author a short PROP documenting the steady state + accepting it. No code change. Optionally tune PROP-130 canary threshold if 1-in-N cycles becomes noise.
part_C_ship_or_follow_up.if_OPT_3_supported: Author PROP with the workspace-sync-side skip logic + PROP-051-class review + fail-open discipline (bug in the pre-check must not block workspace-sync entirely). Propose-only, operator ratifies next session.

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: monitor/tinker/reports/status-json-race-3peat-forensics-2026-07-15.md — 1-page report answering Q1-Q4 with commit SHAs + timestamps + regressed/advanced field lists.
One PROP recommending OPT-1, OPT-2, or OPT-3 with clear reasoning tied back to Part A's evidence.
If PROP recommends OPT-1: include the specific cron changes as a table (agent, current cron, proposed cron, rationale) + operator-copy-paste update_scheduled_task calls.
If PROP recommends OPT-2: include the accepted steady-state rate + criterion that would flip the decision (e.g., '≥5 consecutive days OR ≥10 fires in 30 days → revisit').

constraints.no_actual_schedule_changes_in_this_direc: Investigate + recommend + propose (via PROP). Actual scheduled_tasks update calls are operator action, not tinker action. If tinker recommends OPT-1, tinker provides the specific update payload but operator makes the call.
constraints.prop_051_awareness_for_OPT_3: Any workspace-sync hot-path change (OPT-3) MUST include fail-open discipline: a bug in the pre-check must not halt all workspace-sync pushes. PROP-127 CHECK 3 is the reference pattern.
constraints.do_not_touch_prop_130_canary_thresholds_: The canary is working as designed (detects + attributes + confirms self-heal). Tuning its threshold is only appropriate if OPT-2 wins and only if the current rate genuinely becomes noise.
